messages:
Maria: FYI seeing a sharp tail-latency uptick on runtime v3.2.0 deployed ~10:05 UTC, p95 for /v1/generate jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms for some tenants. Not across the board.
Maria: sample metrics: tenant=acme, model=rw-13b, p95=420ms, p99=1.2s, error rates unchanged.
Lee: reassigning to runtime triage. Which deployment cohort? full-ramp or staged?
Maria: staged rollout -> ~7% traffic, kube-set label runtime=3.2.0 on pool-17. Affected tenants mostly in us-west.
Ash: did we change scheduler or batching defaults in this release? I see a PR that adjusted scheduler heuristics (PR #834).
Lee: Checking changelog... scheduler defaults tuned to prefer larger batches at lower CPU cost. Could increase tail if traffic variance is high.
Tim: Can we reproduce locally with a synthetic fanout? If yes we should try traffic patterns that mimic acme production.
Kara: Customer support: acme raised a ticket, they're seeing occasional 500ms+ waits in UI. They asked for ETA.
Maria: quick traces attached: trace ids: trc_9a2f, trc_f3b1. Stack shows delay in `request_mux` waiting on batch fill for ~300ms before kernel start.
Ash: that smells like batching policy change. If batches are held to reach target size we get fill delay. What are batch_size and batching_window settings in 3.2.0?
Lee: config snippet from the rollout: `batching: target_size: 32, max_wait_ms: 50, dynamic: true` prior was `target_size: 16, max_wait_ms: 10`
Tim: ah, that explains it. For low QPS tenants, larger target_size + longer wait can add tail. Need to either reduce target_size for small tenants or make dynamic threshold per tenant.
Maria: immediate mitigation options?
Ash: 1) Roll back runtime to 3.1.x for the staged group (safest). 2) Hotpatch to restore old batching defaults. 3) Route the small-traffic tenants off the updated pool (traffic-split).
Lee: We can do a quick traffic-split: route tenant=acme traffic to runtime=3.1.9 for now. I can apply a route override.
deploy-bot: Applying route override: route_override set tenant=acme -> runtime=3.1.9. Change id: ro-9123.
Lee: Done. Can someone verify latency for acme now?
Kara: acme confirms initial UI response improved in next 30s to ~150ms. They say much better.
Maria: Observability note: p95 for acme dropped back to ~140ms shortly after override. Global p95 still elevated because other small tenants still on 3.2.0.
Tim: For broader rollback we should coordinate with releases. If hotpatch is needed, we can push a patch to revert batching defaults.
Ash: I can prepare a hotpatch PR to reset `target_size=16` and `max_wait_ms=10` with a feature flag for perf testing.
Lee: Also add a runtime-side adaptive policy: if observed fill latency > 100ms for a tenant, temporarily lower target_size. That would avoid manual routing. File a follow-up.
Maria: Action items: Lee - keep route overrides for affected tenants until rollback/hotpatch. Ash - hotpatch PR + heatmap of tenant QPS to identify vulnerable cohorts. Tim - synthetic repro with low QPS fanout to validate. Kara - keep acme updated.
Tim: Repro steps I used: `wrk -c 50 -t 8 -d 60s --latency http://runtime-3.2.0/p1/generate -H 'x-tenant: acme'` and a small lambda to send bursty single-request patterns. See attached script.
Ash: +1 on capturing flamegraphs around batch fill/eviction. I'll instrument the batching path and collect a couple of samples in staging.
Lee: Postmortem timeline: we should note change in batching defaults + lack of per-tenant adaptive guard -> regression. Add to release checklist: load-profile guardrails for scheduling changes.
Maria: Any objections to rolling 3.2.0 back from staged->full ramp until hotpatch is validated?
Tim: no objections. If releases agrees we should halt ramp and keep flags for rapid rollback.
deploy-bot: Initiating partial rollback: runtime 3.2.0 -> reduce staged pool from 7% -> 0% while preserving canary. Roll id: rb-4412.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete for staged cohort (pool-17). Canary remains at 1%.
Lee: Monitoring p95/p99 across tenants. So far we see normalization for most affected. We'll keep an eye for residuals.
Kara: Customer update to acme: "We routed traffic back to the prior runtime and are monitoring — performance should be improved. We'll follow up with timeline for full fix."
Maria: Follow-ups: prioritize hotpatch + per-tenant adaptive batching logic, update rollout playbook, add automated alert when batch_fill_latency > 100ms for any tenant for >5m.
Ash: I'll own the hotpatch PR and perf tests.
Tim: I'll add repro scripts + synthetic tests to the release gating tests.
Lee: I'll draft a short incident note and tag release and oncall for Friday retro.
Maria: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
